prompt: A photo app stretches a picture taller by TRIPLING every height above the middle line. One point on the picture was $5$ units above the middle line. How many units above the middle line is it now?
hint: Stretching taller works like $3 \cdot f(x)$. What does that do to the height of each point?

hints.text: Stretching taller works like $3 \cdot f(x)$. What does that do to the height of each point?
Tripling means multiplying by $3$, and the old height is $5$ units. Work out $3 \times 5$.
The new height is $3 \times 5 = 15$, so the point is now $15$ units above the middle line.

explanation: A vertical stretch multiplies every height by the same number and leaves left-right positions alone.
The word tripling tells us the multiplier is $3$, and the point started $5$ units above the line.
Multiplying gives $3 \times 5 = 15$, so the point is now $15$ units above the middle line.

alternativeExplanations.title: Two points, one rule
steps: A point 1 unit up moves to 3 units up.
A point 2 units up moves to 6 units up.
The pattern is "times 3" every time, so 5 units up becomes 15 units up.
